text: Files, AI needs a better index, not a bigger model. That is many RAG's whole claim, and if it holds, private retrieval stops being a data center problem and starts being a phone problem. Here is how retrieval augmented

title: How RAG works today
text: Generation works today. Three stages, build an index over your documents, retrieve what looks relevant, generate the answer. Now watch what sits behind all three stages, a large language model doing the understanding at every single step. That is the design assumption. Nobody ever wrote it down. title: What breaks on a small model
text: Small one in. Light RAG falls from 56.9% to 35.4. Graph RAG does not fall, it stops. Every small model, no usable output at all. The paper's table just prints a slash. These systems do not degrade. They were built on an assumption, and the assumption left the room. Which gives the paper its three

title: The paper's three questions
text: Questions. Does many RAG actually beat the alternatives? What is each piece of it contributing? And can it survive a question that needs more than one hop of reasoning? Three questions, three sections, and no hand waving between them. Before the architecture, the receipt.

title: The architecture
text: Stages, but look where the work moved. Indexing builds a graph instead of a pile of text. Retrieval walks that graph in two steps. First, map the query on the entities, then follow the structure to the answer. The model still writes the final sentence. It just stopped doing the thinking.

title: Two nodes, two edges
text: The index is the trick. Two kinds of node, the text chunks themselves and the named entities pulled out of them. Two kinds of edge, entity to entity and entity back to the chunk it came from. Each edge carrying a written description of the relationship. Small models are poor summarizers, but perfectly good entity extractors, so the index only ever asks them for the easy part. Watch

title: A real query, both systems
text: It run on one real question from the paper. Which Italian restaurant are Wolfgang and Lie Hua going to to celebrate his promotion? Light RAG on the same small model hunts for text that matches and returns a pasta joint name not listed. Mini RAG guesses the answer type first, this is a location. Then it walks the graph to the location that connects both people and the promotion. Venedig Grandcaf. Across every small

title: The results
text: Model they tested, same story. Phi-3.5, 39.8 up to 53.3. GLM Edge, a 1.5 billion parameter model, 35.7 up to 52.5. That last one matters most, the smallest model in the set gains the most between 1.3 and 2.5 times the effectiveness of the lightweight systems it replaces.

title: Take the index out
text: But a results table only tells you that it works, not why, so they took it apart. Remove the edge descriptions, accuracy slips three points. Remove the chunk nodes, four points. Replace the heterogeneous index with ordinary description-based indexing and it collapses from 53 to 26. Half the system's performance lives in the index, that is the claim tested. Now the part

title: Where it bites
text: The paper does not dwell on. On the harder multi-hop benchmark, Mini RAG nearly doubles Light RAG's accuracy, 50 compared to 27. But look at the error rate underneath. Light RAG is wrong 11.8% of the time, Mini RAG 28.4. It answers far more questions and it is confidently wrong far more often. If you are building on this, that trade is yours to price. So why care? title: Verdict
text: Contribution is not a better model, it is a better place to put the work. The ablation is the evidence, pull the index out and half the performance goes with it. It buys you on-device private retrieval at quarter of the storage and it costs you a higher error rate on hard questions, which the paper never quite says out loud. Your turn. Paste this. I

title: Your turn
text: Want to test whether mini RAG's core claim holds on my own data. Help me design a small experiment. One, pick a document set I already have. Two, define 10 questions where the answer needs two hops. Three, tell me what accuracy and what error rate would make me believe the index is doing the work, not the model. Then check the answer against three things. Does it separate accuracy from error rate? Does it name a baseline to compare against? And does it tell you what result would prove the claim wrong? If it skips that third one, push back. Mini RAG, the index does the thinking. Lay them in for bear.
